_help: Benchmarks shown beside your speaking metrics in the report. 'min' and 'max' set the target range (leave one out if there is only a limit one way). Edit freely. These come from public sales research (see 'sources') and are guides, not laws. Last researched: October 2026 - re-check occasionally.

sources.label: Gong Labs - analysis of 100k cold calls (talk ratio, longest monologue, call length)
Gong - best and worst cold call openers (300M calls)
Gong - what top sellers do differently in discovery (talk ratio, number of questions)
Gong Labs - filler words in sales (no link to win rates)
Hyperbound - speaking pace benchmark (about 150 words per minute)

talk_share.label: Talk time (you)
talk_share.note: In Gong's data, reps in successful cold calls talk about 55% of the time. A cold call needs more rep talk than discovery, but it should still be a conversation.

wpm.label: Speaking pace
wpm.note: Hyperbound's benchmark is about 150. Below ~120 can sound disengaged; above ~160 people follow less. Estimated from how long you spoke.

filler_pct.label: Filler words
filler_pct.note: A common coaching target. Gong's own analysis of nearly 500,000 calls found no link between filler words and winning, so treat this as polish, not a priority. Speech-to-text often drops fillers, so the count is a minimum.

longest_monologue_s.label: Longest stretch talking
longest_monologue_s.note: Gong: top reps keep any continuous stretch under ~76 seconds. In successful cold calls the longest stretch averaged about 53 s (vs 25 s in failed ones), because a good pitch earns attention. Just don't ramble.

questions.label: Questions you asked
questions.note: A typical cold call is a ~30-second opener, a value statement, 2–3 qualifying questions, then a direct ask.

talk_share.label: Talk time (you)
talk_share.target: 55% or less (43% is the classic ideal)
talk_share.note: The classic benchmark is 43% rep / 57% prospect. Gong's 2025 analysis of 326,000 calls found the average rep talks about 60%, with won deals at 57% and lost deals at 62%.

wpm.label: Speaking pace
wpm.note: Hyperbound's benchmark is about 150. Slow down for pricing and complex points (100–120); a little faster is fine for stories. Estimated from how long you spoke.

filler_pct.label: Filler words
filler_pct.note: A common coaching target. Gong found no link between filler words and winning, so treat this as polish. Speech-to-text often drops fillers, so the count is a minimum.

longest_monologue_s.label: Longest stretch talking
longest_monologue_s.note: Gong: top reps keep any continuous stretch under ~76 seconds. In discovery, long stretches usually mean pitching instead of asking.

questions.label: Questions you asked
questions.note: Gong's older data says 11–14; its 2025 data has won deals at about 15–16 questions and lost deals at about 20. Spread them through the call instead of firing them off as a checklist.
